title: Adding, subtracting and multiplying complex numbers
keyIdea: To add or subtract complex numbers, combine the real parts and the imaginary parts separately: (a + bi) ± (c + di) = (a ± c) + (b ± d)i. To multiply, expand all four products and use i² = −1: (a + bi)(c + di) = (ac − bd) + (ad + bc)i. On an Argand diagram, adding is placing arrows tip to tail, multiplying by i is a 90° turn about O, and in any product the moduli multiply and the arguments add.

visual.caption: Is the answer real or does it have an imaginary part? Work it out, then drag each card, or tap it and then a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: add and subtract by dragging w on an Argand diagram, turn z by multiplying by i, expand (2 + 3i)(4 − i) in a grid, and land zw on 4i.

kid: A complex number has a real part and an imaginary part, like 3 + 2i. To add two of them, add the real parts and add the imaginary parts. So (3 + 2i) + (1 − 5i) = 4 − 3i.
To subtract, take away each part. The minus sign acts on both parts of the second number: (5 + i) − (2 − 3i) = 5 − 2 + i + 3i = 3 + 4i.
To multiply, expand the brackets as in algebra. There are four products. Then use the rule i² = −1. For example, (2 + 3i)(4 − i) = 8 − 2i + 12i − 3i². Since −3i² = +3, the answer is 11 + 10i.
On an Argand diagram, z + w puts the arrow for w on the tip of the arrow for z. Times i turns a point 90° anticlockwise about 0. In any product, the lengths multiply and the angles add.
adult: Ages 16 to 18. Edexcel A level Further Maths (9FM0), Core Pure 1, asks students to add, subtract and multiply complex numbers in the form x + iy. They must also show sums and differences on an Argand diagram. AQA 7367 covers the same work. The rules |zw| = |z||w| and arg(zw) = arg z + arg w come later in the course. The lab gives a first look at them.

Students already know how to expand two brackets. The only new step is i² = −1. It makes the bd term real and negative: (a + bi)(c + di) = (ac − bd) + (ad + bc)i. Ask them to write all four products before they simplify.

Common mistakes: using i² = +1, which gives 5 + 10i instead of 11 + 10i; dropping the two cross terms; taking the minus off only the real part of the second number; leaving i² in an answer; and adding moduli when they should multiply. Be careful with signs when d is negative.

In the lab, students drag w on a grid until z + w, then z − w, land on a target. They multiply by i and watch a quarter turn. They fill a grid for (2 + 3i)(4 − i) and use i² = −1. Last, they find w so that (1 + i)w = 4i, and read the moduli and angles as they go.

practice.prompt: (a + 3i) + (5 − 7i) = x + yi with a = {a}. What is x?
practice.hint: Add the real parts only: a and 5.
practice.explain: Real parts add: {a} + 5 = {=a+5}. The imaginary part is 3 − 7 = −4.

practice.prompt: (2 + {b}i)(1 + i) = x + yi. What is x, the real part?
practice.explain: The real terms are 2 and {b}i² = −{b}, so x = 2 − {b} = {=2-b}. The imaginary part is 2 + {b}.

practice.hint: The minus acts on both parts: −(2 − 3i) = −2 + 3i.
practice.explain: 5 − 2 = 3 and 1 − (−3) = 4, so the answer is 3 + 4i. 3 − 2i forgets to change the sign of −3i.

practice.hint: Four products: 3, i, 6i and 2i². Then i² = −1.
practice.explain: 3 + i + 6i + 2i² = 3 − 2 + 7i = 1 + 7i. 5 + 7i treats i² as +1; 3 + 2i drops the cross terms.

practice.prompt: On an Argand diagram, what does multiplying z by i do?
choices: Reflects z in the real axis
practice.hint: Try i(3 + i) = −1 + 3i and plot both points.
practice.explain: i(a + bi) = −b + ai, a quarter turn anticlockwise with the same modulus. Moving up by 1 is adding i.

pool.hint: Expand, and watch the cross terms cancel.
pool.explain: 4 − 2i + 2i − i² = 4 + 1 = 5, a real number. 3 uses i² = +1; 4 − i² is not simplified.

pool.hint: Add real parts, then add imaginary parts with their signs.
pool.explain: 3 + 1 = 4 and 2 + (−5) = −3, so 4 − 3i. Adding never creates an i² term.

pool.hint: In a product, the moduli multiply.
pool.explain: |zw| = |z| × |w| = {p} × 3 = {=3*p}. Adding them would give the wrong length.

pool.hint: Expand to 2i + 5i², then replace i² with −1.

pool.prompt: A student writes (a + bi)(c + di) = ac + bdi. What went wrong?
choices: They multiplied parts pairwise and dropped the cross terms
They should have added a and c
pool.hint: How many terms does expanding two brackets give?
pool.explain: There are four products: ac + adi + bci + bdi² = (ac − bd) + (ad + bc)i.

pool.hint: i⁴ = i² × i², or four quarter turns.
pool.explain: i² × i² = (−1)(−1) = 1. Four 90° turns bring a point back to where it started.
